rationale: A 50-year-old male with fulminant necrotising amoebic colitis of the entire colon requiring total colectomy. Histopathology of the colectomy specimen demonstrated pathogenic Entamoeba trophozoites with ingested erythrocytes (erythrophagocytosis), which is E1 confirmatory. Amoebic serology was also strongly positive for IgM antibodies (E2). All VPD criteria met -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Pathogenic Entamoebae trophozoites were recognized by the presence of phagocytosed ingested intracellular red cells.
Amoebic serology was positive with high IgM antibody titers (2.24) <0.04.

rationale: A 78-year-old male presenting with sepsis secondary to a large left hepatic lobe abscess. Percutaneous drainage yielded purulent fluid growing Klebsiella pneumoniae, and serum ELISA serology was positive for Entamoeba histolytica antibodies (E2). The clinical team established a diagnosis of bacterial superinfection of an underlying amoebic liver abscess and successfully treated with ceftriaxone, metronidazole, and paromomycin -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: While a stool ova and parasite examination on the patient was negative, further workup revealed that the patient was positive for Entamoeba histolytica antibody in the serum, detected via enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay and indicative of either current or prior infection.

rationale: A 55-year-old male with acute necrotizing colitis, septic shock, and disseminated abscesses in the liver, kidney, retroperitoneum, and thigh. Histological analysis of the right colon demonstrated extensive mucosal/submucosal ulcerations covered by Entamoeba histolytica trophozoites (E1), and amoebic serology was strongly positive by both latex agglutination (1:32) and ELISA (5 AU) (E2). VPD criteria fully met -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Histological analysis of the right colon showed many ulcerations of the mucosa and submucosa, covered by many Entamoeba histolytic.
Serology for E. histolytica was positive [Latex test: 1/32, positivity threshold >1/5; ELISA: 5 Arbitrary Unit (AU), positivity threshold> 1.1 AU].

rationale: A 57-year-old male with Crohn's disease on infliximab presenting with cyclic fevers, night sweats, and RUQ pain. CT demonstrated two large hypoenhancing liver lesions (9.2 cm and 3.5 cm). Diagnostic Entamoeba histolytica enzyme immunoassay (EIA) returned positive results. Percutaneous drainage and treatment with metronidazole followed by paromomycin resulted in complete clinical and radiological resolution. Meets E2 strong evidence criteria (positive amebic EIA with CT-confirmed liver abscess cavities) and all VPD criteria -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Computed tomography (CT) of the abdomen and pelvis revealed two hypoenhancing lesions in the liver measuring 9.2 cm and 3.5 cm consistent with pyogenic liver abscesses (PLA) (Figures 1 and 2).
On day seven of hospitalization, the Entamoeba histolytica enzyme immunoassay returned positive results.

rationale: A 65-year-old male with persistent fever, chills, and right hypochondriac pain following travel to Liberia. Abdominal CT scan confirmed hepatic abscesses. Specific serological blood testing for Entamoeba histolytica antibodies was positive. The abscess was drained and treated with IV metronidazole for 14 days, resulting in complete clinical recovery. Meets E2 strong evidence criteria (positive amebic serology in a patient with CT-confirmed hepatic abscess) and all VPD criteria -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The smears returned negative, and the CT scan revealed liver abscesses (Figures 1 and 2); thus, further tests were required.
A blood test was performed searching for Echinococcus granulosus antibodies and Entamoeba histolytica antibodies, and the test rendered positive results for Entamoeba histolytica.

rationale: A 72-year-old male presenting with hepatic abscesses 22 years after visiting Senegal. Diagnostic aspiration of the liver abscess was performed, and in-house Entamoeba histolytica real-time PCR was positive, providing definitive E1 confirmatory evidence. Amebic serology was also strongly positive by both ELISA IgG (8.72; threshold 0.9) and latex agglutination (E2). The patient achieved clinical recovery following metronidazole and tiliquinol-tilbroquinol therapy. All criteria for confirmed VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: This in-house PCR test was positive, thus confirming the diagnosis of ALA.

However, amebiasis serology by ELISA Ridascreen E. histolytica IgG, (R-Biopharm GmbH, Darmstadt, Germany) was positive (IgG: 8.72; threshold: 0.9), as was latex agglutination (Bichro-Latex Amibe Fumouze, Fumouze Diagnostics, Levallois-Perret, France).
evidence_items.test_name: Amebiasis ELISA IgG and latex agglutination serology

rationale: A 28-year-old male with Crohn's disease and recent travel to India presenting with acute right upper quadrant pain and fever. Abdominal CT demonstrated a 6.0 cm x 5.0 cm hepatic abscess cavity in segment 4A/B, and bacterial/fungal cultures from percutaneous aspiration were sterile. Serum Entamoeba histolytica IgG antibody returned positive (E2), and the patient demonstrated rapid, near-complete abscess resolution following metronidazole therapy. E2 strong evidence criteria in conjunction with characteristic CT abscess cavity and clinical response confirm amebic liver abscess -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Entamoeba histolytica IgG antibody returned positive three days after discharge, supporting the diagnosis of amebic liver abscess.

Computed tomography (CT) scan of the abdomen/pelvis showed a 6.0 cm x 5.0 cm low/intermediate density lesion in segment 4A/B of the liver with a thick marginal rim and adjacent parenchymal inflammation and biliary prominence (Figure 1).

rationale: A 36-year-old female presenting with septic shock, generalized peritonitis, and toxic megacolon requiring emergent laparotomy and total colectomy. Histopathological examination of the total colectomy surgical specimen demonstrated fulminant amoebic (Entamoeba histolytica) colitis with extensive mucosal ulcerations and transmural perforation (E1/E2 confirmatory histopathology). Coinfection with Trichuris trichiura and Taenia solium was noted. The patient was treated with intravenous metronidazole, oral albendazole, and praziquantel, and made a complete recovery. VPD criteria confirmed -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Histopathology analysis of the total colectomy specimen showed there was fulminant amoebic (Entamoeba histolytica) colitis resulting in ulceration and perforation of the colon.
evidence_items.test_name: Histopathological examination of total colectomy specimen

evidence_items.source_quote: An emergent laparotomy performed revealed grossly dilated colon with numerous areas of ulceration and perforation resulting in faeculant peritonitis.

rationale: A 6-year-old male child presenting with fever, loose motions, and hepatomegaly found to have a large left hepatic lobe abscess extending with thrombus into the IVC and right atrium. Amebic serology by ELISA was positive, and emergency surgical de-roofing drained 100 ml of characteristic anchovy sauce pus. Responded to metronidazole and surgical evacuation with full recovery at 6 months. High-titer amebic serology with CT-confirmed hepatic abscess and anchovy-sauce aspirate satisfies E2 strong evidence and VPD criteria -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient tested positive for amebic antibody by Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) test.
About 100 ml of anchovy sauce pus was drained from the abscess cavity.
evidence_items.target_concept: Amoebic liver abscess anchovy sauce pus

rationale: A 22-year-old male presenting with high fever, cough with brownish-red sputum, hepatomegaly, and altered mental status. Abdominal CT revealed a massive 750 cc right hepatic lobe abscess ruptured into the subdiaphragmatic space, and brain MRI revealed multiple ring-enhancing brain abscesses. Entamoeba histolytica IgG ELISA (RIDASCREEN) was positive, confirming amebic liver and brain abscesses. The patient responded to parenteral and oral metronidazole with near total radiological resolution and complete neurological recovery. High-titer specific amebic serology with confirmed hepatic abscess satisfies E2 strong evidence and VPD criteria -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: His enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay test for Entamoeba histolytica immunoglobulin G was done with RIDASCREEN kit from r-Biopharm (Darmstadt, Germany), which was reported positive, suggesting amebic etiology of liver and brain abscesses.

Abdominal ultrasound and contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) scan of the thorax and abdomen revealed a single large abscess of approximately 750 cc volume in the right lobe of the liver with evidence of rupture into the right subdiaphragmatic space

rationale: A 45-year-old male presenting with intermittent bloody diarrhea and abdominal pain after residing in Indonesia. Emergency colonoscopy demonstrated multiple indurated ulcerations over the rectum and cecum. Histopathological examination with periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) stain confirmed focal aggregations of amoeba trophozoites in the lamina propria, diagnostic of ameboma and invasive amebic dysentery. Following treatment with metronidazole and iodoquinol, symptoms resolved within 3 days, and follow-up colonoscopy demonstrated complete mucosal remission. Colonoscopic demonstration of typical mucosal ulcers with trophozoites on histopathology satisfies E2 strong evidence and VPD criteria -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Colonoscopy was also done at the emergency room and showed multiple small polyps over the terminal ileum and multiple indurated ulcerations over the rectum and cecum (fig. 1).
Focal aggregations of amoeba trophozoites were demonstrated by periodic acid-Schiff stain (fig. 2). Ameboma was diagnosed and metronidazole was prescribed for invasive dysentery for 14 days.

rationale: A 46-year-old male with poorly controlled diabetes presenting with fever, chills, RUQ pain, and diarrhea. Abdominal CT revealed an 8.5 x 9.6 x 6.8 cm complex abscess in the left hepatic lobe with concomitant colitis and IVC/hepatic vein thrombosis. Specific serum antibody for Entamoeba histolytica was positive, confirming amebic liver abscess. The patient completed a 10-day course of metronidazole followed by paromomycin luminal therapy with resolution of fever, abdominal pain, and liver enzymes. High-titer specific amebic serology in a patient with CT-confirmed hepatic abscess cavity satisfies E2 strong evidence and VPD criteria -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: He remained hospitalized for twelve days, during which time serum antibody for Entameba histolytica was positive (confirming diagnosis) and AFP and CEA were found to be within normal limits ruling out possible malignancy.

At this time, amebic liver abscess was the leading differential; hence, he was admitted and started on metronidazole 500 mg intravenously every eight hours along with warfarin bridged with unfractionated heparin for pulmonary emboli.

rationale: A 73-year-old female presenting with severe acute abdominal pain and peritonitis resulting in colonic perforation requiring emergency total colectomy. Preoperative colonic mucosal biopsy revealed parasitic bodies with ingested erythrocytes suggestive of Entamoeba histolytica trophozoites. Definitive histopathological examination of the total colectomy surgical specimen demonstrated extensive mucosal ulceration and transmural necrosis with E. histolytica trophozoites packed with phagocytosed red blood cells (erythrophagocytosis) throughout the entire bowel wall. Microscopic demonstration of E. histolytica trophozoites displaying erythrophagocytosis in tissue biopsy and surgical resection fulfills E1 confirmatory criteria and satisfies all VPD requirements -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Sections under the microscope showed fragments of colonic mucosa with ulceration of the epithelium and a lymphoplasmacytic infiltration with eosinophiles, accompanied with edema, congestion, hemorrhage, and parasitic bodies with phagocyted red blood cells suggestive of E. histolytica trophozoites.
E. histolytica trophozoites loaded with red blood cells were recognized in the entire bowel wall (Figure 3).

rationale: A 31-year-old HIV-infected male presenting with a massive hepatic abscess (19.3 x 16.5 cm) yielding characteristic jam-like fluid and right-sided pleural effusion. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) of the liver abscess aspirate detected specific sequence reads of amoeba trophozoites (E1 molecular confirmatory), and histopathological examination of liver tissue confirmed amoeba trophozoites (E1/E2). The patient achieved clinical cure following metronidazole therapy. All VPD criteria met -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Later, we sent the liver abscess fluid for mNGS detection. It reported sequence reads of amoeba trophozoites (specific sequence reads: 81).

The final pathological feedback confirmed the presence of amoeba trophozoites in the tissue (Figure 1D). As a result, the patient's diagnosis was determined as amoebic liver abscess, amoebic pulmonary abscess, and concurrent HIV infection.
evidence_items.test_name: Histopathological examination of resected liver tissue

evidence_items.source_quote: Percutaneous drainage was performed for the liver abscess and a jam-like turbid fluid was extracted (Figure 1B).

rationale: A 28-year-old male presenting with a ruptured hepatic abscess (11.5 x 6.3 cm) communicating into the right pleural cavity. Diagnostic evaluation demonstrated positive Entamoeba histolytica antigen in the brown pleural drainage fluid (E1 disease-defining/confirmatory) and strongly positive amoebic IgG serology (43.7 NTU [<9], E2 strong evidence). Clinical and radiological resolution followed drainage and targeted antimicrobial therapy. All VPD criteria met -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The content obtained from the drainage was tested for the Entamoeba histolytica antigen - positive result.
In addition, the diagnostics was performed with the serology of amoebiasis (Immunoglobulin G antibody positive with the 43.7 NTU [<9] activity).
A chest CT (computed tomography) scan performed 3 days after admission revealed a thick-walled fluid lesion measuring 11.5x6.3 cm in the right lobe of the liver

rationale: A 66-year-old male presenting with rectal bleeding and mucus discharge found to have rectal ulcerations on flexible sigmoidoscopy. Histopathological examination of the rectal biopsy on PAS stain demonstrated amoebic trophozoites with ingested red blood cells (erythrophagocytosis), which is E1 disease-defining/confirmatory for Entamoeba histolytica colitis/proctitis. The patient completely resolved on metronidazole. All VPD criteria met -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Associated with the fibrin on the surface of the mucosa there were occasional amoebic trophozoites, some with ingested red blood cells within their cytoplasm (Figure 2).
evidence_items.target_concept: Entamoeba histolytica trophozoites with ingested RBCs

evidence_items.source_quote: Histological findings on PAS (Periodic acid-Schiff) staining revealed features of amoebic proctitis.

rationale: A 61-year-old male originally from Nigeria presenting with fever, RUQ pain, and a large solitary right hepatic lobe abscess (13.93 x 9.17 cm) on ultrasound and CT. Percutaneous catheter drainage was performed, and serological testing was positive for Entamoeba histolytica (E2 strong evidence satisfying diagnostic criteria for amoebic liver abscess). The patient was treated with intravenous metronidazole followed by luminal paromomycin, with follow-up CT at 3 months confirming near-complete abscess resolution. All VPD criteria met -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The abscess was later identified as amebic in origin after the serological testing came back positive for E. histolytica, leading to the addition of paromomycin (1,000 mg every eight hours) for seven days to the treatment regimen.
A computed tomography (CT) of the abdomen and pelvis further characterized this lesion as measuring 13.93 cm x 9.17 cm, suggestive of a significant liver abscess (Figure 2).

rationale: A 46-year-old female healthcare worker presenting with chronic constipation and rectal bleeding, with CT and MRI revealing a massive distal rectal wall thickening concerning for rectal adenocarcinoma. Rectoscopy and colonoscopy biopsy with histopathological examination ruled out malignancy and demonstrated protozoa consistent with amoeba (E2). The patient was treated with metronidazole and paromomycin with complete radiological and symptomatic resolution of the ameboma. VPD criteria met -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Nevertheless, the histopathological assessment of several biopsies obtained during the procedure did not reveal any abnormal cells suggestive of malignant conditions; instead, protozoa consistent with amoeba were observed.
The histopathological evaluation of the colonoscopy biopsy ruled out malignancy and confirmed the diagnosis of intestinal amoebiasis, prompting the initiation of specific treatment.
evidence_items.test_name: Colonoscopy biopsy histopathology confirming intestinal amoebiasis

rationale: A 58-year-old female presenting with right-sided chest pain, fever, weight loss, and history of travel to Mexico, found on CT to have a large solitary 14 x 10 x 13 cm liver abscess cavity draining 500 mL of grayish purulent fluid. Serology for Entamoeba histolytica IgG antibodies was positive (E2), while aspirate and blood cultures were sterile. Treatment with oral metronidazole produced prompt clinical and radiologic improvement, confirming amebic liver abscess. VPD criteria met -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: serology for Entamoeba histolytica was performed and came back positive for E. histolytica IgG antibodies.

evidence_items.source_quote: A subsequent CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast (Figure 2) confirmed a lobulated, hypodense, non-cystic lesion measuring 14 x 10 x 13 cm.
evidence_items.test_name: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast showing large liver abscess

rationale: A 47-year-old female with chronic kidney disease presenting with multiple erythematous-violaceous nodular skin lesions and subcutaneous abscesses spreading from a subclavian catheter insertion site. Fine-needle aspiration demonstrated cysts and trophozoites of Entamoeba histolytica on direct microscopy, and skin biopsy histopathology confirmed histiocytic inflammation with Entamoeba histolytica trophozoites in the superficial and deep dermis (E1). The lesions resolved after oral metronidazole and ivermectin, confirming cutaneous amoebiasis -> POSITIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: A skin biopsy was also performed, and histopathology showed an histiocytic reaction surrounding abscesses in the superficial and deep dermis, with trophozoites of Entamoeba histolytica identified on high power microscopy (Fig. 3).

rationale: A 54-year-old male presenting with a large liver abscess initially treated empirically with eravacycline and percutaneous drainage. Stool antigen testing returned positive for Entamoeba histolytica (E1 confirmatory), establishing amebic liver abscess, and prompting transition to standard-of-care oral metronidazole. VPD criteria met -> POSITIVE.

When Entamoeba histolytica stool antigen testing returned positive (E1 confirmatory), eravacycline was discontinued and standard of care metronidazole (750 mg PO every 8 h) was initiated, keeping the patient afebrile. VPD criteria met -> POSITIVE.

rationale: A 2-year-and-11-month-old female toddler presenting with prolonged high fever, periumbilical abdominal pain, hepatomegaly, and a large liver abscess, initially misdiagnosed as incomplete Kawasaki disease. Surgical drainage and partial hepatectomy were performed; immunohistochemical analysis of liver necrotic tissue demonstrated amebic trophozoites (E1 confirmatory), establishing amebic liver abscess (ALA). The patient achieved complete recovery following metronidazole therapy. VPD criteria met -> POSITIVE.

rationale: A 29-year-old female in Burundi presenting with sepsis, RUQ abdominal pain, and marked hepatic tenderness following emergency cesarean delivery. Ultrasound demonstrated an 11 x 12 cm liver abscess cavity draining 200 mL of characteristic anchovy paste pus. Direct microscopic examination of the aspirated pus revealed Entamoeba histolytica (E1/E2). Systemic and local metronidazole therapy led to complete resolution. VPD criteria met -> POSITIVE.

rationale: A 43-year-old male with HIV infection presenting with fever, RUQ pain, and a large liver abscess complicated by rupture into the pleural space with 'fish sauce-like' pleural effusion. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) of both pleural and liver abscess drainage fluids detected Entamoeba histolytica sequences (E1 confirmatory), and wet mount microscopy of liver aspirate showed amebic trophozoites with pseudopods. Co-infection with Salmonella Typhi was also identified, and the patient responded successfully to metronidazole, paromomycin, and ceftriaxone -> POSITIVE.
